system:
You are working out the chronology of a compulsory third party motor accident claim in New South Wales, from a list of things recorded about decided claims.

Divide the life of a claim into ordered PHASES, and place every recorded item in the phase at which the thing it measures COMES INTO EXISTENCE -- not when it is written down, and not when it is used.

That distinction decides most of the hard cases:
  * A medical assessment performed years later measures a physical state that arose at the time of the injury. Ask when the QUANTITY was fixed, not when it was measured.
  * Something recorded in the final decision may describe a fact established long before it.
  * A procedural fact about how the claim was run belongs to the phase in which the claim was run, not to the injury.

Decide how many phases there are. Use as few as genuinely capture the order and no more; a phase containing one item is fine if that item really stands alone in time. Items that arise at the same stage belong in the same phase, and a phase may contain items that cause one another -- being contemporaneous is not being simultaneous.

For every item, say in one sentence WHEN the thing it measures came into existence. That sentence is the justification for its placement and will be recorded.
user:
Recorded about each decided claim:
  - Lump Sum: the total dollar amount awarded to the claimant
  - WPI %: whole person impairment as a percentage, from a medical assessment
  - Non-Economic Loss: dollars awarded for non-economic loss (pain and suffering)
  - Future Economic Loss: dollars awarded for future loss of earning capacity
  - Claimant Weekly Income: the claimant's pre-accident weekly earnings, in dollars
  - Claimant Age: the claimant's age at the date of injury, in years
  - Claimant Gender: the claimant's recorded gender
  - Nature: the procedural route the claim took: settlement approval, or damages assessment
  - Injury Burden Intensity: ordinal score for the overall physical burden of the injuries
  - Treatment Burden: ordinal score for the extent of treatment, surgery and ongoing care
  - Work Impact Severity: ordinal score for loss of working capacity
  - Legal Procedural Complexity: ordinal score for procedural complexity of the proceeding
  - Psychological Injury Emphasis: ordinal score for weight given to psychological injury
  - Liability Clarity: ordinal score for how clear fault is
  - Causation Complexity: ordinal score for difficulty attributing the condition to the accident
  - Pre-existing Condition Salience: ordinal score for how prominent a prior condition is

Define the ordered phases of a claim, then place every item in one.

phases.name: Accident Occurrence
phases.description: The phase where personal details of the claimant and the nature of their injury come into existence.

phases.name: Post-Accident Assessment
phases.description: The phase where the impact of the injury and its treatment are quantified.

phases.name: Claims Processing
phases.description: The phase where the procedural aspects of the claim are determined and navigated.

phases.name: Claim Resolution
phases.description: The phase where monetary awards for the claim are calculated and finalized.

assignments.when_it_arises: The claimant's pre-accident weekly earnings are determined by their income before the accident.
The claimant's age is fixed at the time of the accident.
The claimant's gender is a pre-existing personal detail.
The overall physical burden of the injuries is assessed after the accident based on medical evaluations.
The extent of treatment and ongoing care is assessed after the accident through medical consultation.
The loss of working capacity is evaluated after the accident, impacting future work life.
Whole person impairment percentage is assessed post-accident through medical evaluation.
The emphasis on psychological injury is determined based on post-accident assessments.
The clarity of fault is determined during the claims processing phase through legal investigation.
The complexity of attributing the condition to the accident is evaluated during claims processing.
The prominence of any pre-existing conditions is assessed during the claim to determine their impact on the current condition.
This is assessed during the navigation of the claims process based on procedural challenges.
The procedural route of the claim is determined during the claims processing.
The total dollar amount is calculated and awarded finalizing the claim settlement.
The monetary value for pain and suffering is determined during the resolution of the claim.
Predicted future earnings loss is calculated and awarded during the claim resolution.
